recipes.title: Coffee Crème Brûlée
recipes.description: Sous vide method using instant coffee for clean dispersion and no infusion step. More forgiving than the oven, perfectly even texture, holds in the bath if dinner runs late.

steps.title: Preheat the bath
steps.content: Preheat sous vide bath to 176°F (80°C). Set out six 4 oz wide-mouth mason jars with lids and rings.

steps.title: Heat cream and dissolve coffee
steps.content: In a saucepan over medium-low, warm the cream until steaming (do not boil). Off heat, whisk in the instant coffee until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Whisk the yolks
steps.content: In a medium bowl, whisk the yolks, sugar, and salt until pale and ribbony.

steps.title: Temper
steps.content: Whisking constantly, stream the hot coffee cream into the yolks slowly — first tablespoon at a time, then build up.

steps.title: Finish the base
steps.content: Whisk in the vanilla. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a pourable vessel. Skim any foam.

steps.title: Fill the jars
steps.content: Divide custard among the 6 jars, leaving ½ inch of headspace. Cap with lids and rings — finger-tight only.

steps.title: Sous vide
steps.content: Lower jars into the 176°F bath. Cook for 1 hour.

steps.title: Ice bath and chill
steps.content: Transfer to an ice bath for 15 minutes. Refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

steps.title: Brûlée and serve
steps.content: Sprinkle 1 tbsp of turbinado sugar evenly across each. Torch in tight circles until deep amber. Rest 1 minute.

notes.title: Why 176°F / 80°C
notes.body: Sweet spot for crème brûlée texture — yolks set without scrambling, no skin, no grain.

notes.title: Holding tolerance
notes.body: Up to 90 min in the bath is fine, 2 hours max.

notes.title: Instant coffee dosing
notes.body: 1 tbsp = mild. 2 tbsp = balanced. 3 tbsp = strong. Best brands: Mount Hagen, Starbucks VIA Italian Roast, Nescafé Gold, Waka.

notes.title: Make-ahead
notes.body: Custards hold 3 days in the fridge before brûlée. Don't torch until serving.

recipes.title: Mexican Meat Slop
recipes.description: A workhorse — tacos, burritos, nachos, or over rice. Sun-dried tomatoes and chipotles do the heavy lifting.

ingredients.name: chipotle peppers in adobo (chopped, with sauce)

steps.title: Sweat the onion
steps.content: Cook diced onion in a pan over medium heat until softened and translucent, ~3 min.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.content: Add ground beef, break up with a spoon, brown fully.

steps.title: Add spices
steps.content: Add cumin, paprika, garlic powder, taco seasoning, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.

steps.title: Add aromatics
steps.content: Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and chipotles with adobo sauce. Cook 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.content: Pour in beef stock, simmer 5–7 minutes until liquid is mostly absorbed. Taste and adjust seasoning.

notes.title: Serving
notes.body: Great for tacos, burritos, nachos, or over rice.

notes.title: Heat dial
notes.body: Two chipotles = noticeable warmth. Bump to three if you want sweat.

recipes.title: Protein Mashed Potatoes
recipes.description: Yukon Golds with cottage cheese and Fairlife doing the protein work. Ricer, not mixer — gluey potatoes are a tragedy.

ingredients.name: sour cream or lite cream cheese

steps.title: Boil
steps.content: Boil potatoes and whole garlic cloves in well-salted water until fork-tender, ~15–20 min.

steps.title: Drain and dry
steps.content: Drain. Return to hot pot for a minute to evaporate residual water.

steps.title: Blend dairy
steps.content: Blend cottage cheese, Fairlife, sour cream (or lite cream cheese), and butter until completely smooth — no curds.

steps.title: Rice
steps.content: Pass potatoes and softened garlic through a ricer back into the pot.

steps.title: Fold and season
steps.content: Fold in the smooth dairy mixture. Season with salt, white pepper, and onion salt to taste.

notes.title: Texture rule
notes.body: Ricer only. Hand mixer breaks the starch and turns this into glue.

notes.title: Critical step
notes.body: Dairy mixture must be blended completely smooth before folding in. No shortcuts.

notes.title: White pepper
notes.body: Keeps the color clean and adds a subtle, earthy heat that pairs well with the creaminess.

recipes.title: Carne Asada
recipes.description: Thin-sliced cross rib with citrus, cilantro, and a non-traditional splash of soy for umami. Cast iron, screaming hot.

steps.title: Make marinade
steps.content: Whisk all marinade ingredients together. Add meat, coat well.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.content: Refrigerate 2–3 hours. Max 4 — citrus starts breaking down texture beyond that.

steps.title: Temper
steps.content: Pull from fridge, pat dry, rest at room temp 15 minutes.

steps.title: Sear
steps.content: Cast iron screaming hot. 2 minutes per side for deep char.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.content: Rest 5 minutes. Slice against the grain. Finish with fresh lime and reserved cilantro.

notes.title: Soy sauce
notes.body: Adds umami depth without making it taste Asian. Trust the process.

notes.title: Heat matters
notes.body: If the pan isn't smoking, the meat steams instead of searing. Wait for it.

recipes.title: Ken's Egg Salad
recipes.description: Diced precise (¼"), Dijon-forward, with homemade pickled celery and onions doing the work. Self-referential — pulls from your pickled celery recipe.

steps.title: Boil and dice
steps.content: Hard boil eggs, peel, and dice into ¼-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.content: In a medium bowl, combine mayonnaise and Dijon mustard. Mix until smooth.

steps.title: Fold in eggs
steps.content: Add diced eggs to the dressing and fold gently to coat.

steps.title: Season
steps.content: Season with salt, pepper, celery salt, garlic salt, onion salt, and paprika. Stir to combine.

steps.title: Add mix-ins
steps.content: Fold in diced hot pickles, pickled celery, and pickled onions.

steps.title: Rest
steps.content: Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour to allow flavors to combine before serving.

notes.title: Milder version
notes.body: Substitute regular dill pickles for Grillo's Hot.

notes.title: Self-referential
notes.body: This consumes your homemade pickled celery and onions — the pantry ecosystem at work.

recipes.title: Asian-Inspired Ground Beef Stir-Fry
recipes.description: A quick, savory weeknight stir-fry with Yoshida's marinade and Momofuku Chili Crunch, served over rice.

ingredients.name: Momofuku Chili Crunch chili oil, to taste
salt, pepper, garlic salt, to taste

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.content: Sear the ground beef in a hot pan until golden brown. Season with salt, pepper, and garlic salt.

steps.title: Add shallots
steps.content: Add the sliced shallots and stir to combine.

steps.title: Add carrots
steps.content: Add the carrots and stir.

steps.title: Add cabbage
steps.content: Add the cabbage mix last and stir. Let everything cook down until the vegetables are tender.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.content: Pour in the Mr. Yoshida's sauce and let it come to a boil, allowing some liquid to cook off.

steps.title: Vinegar
steps.content: Add the rice vinegar and stir. Let the sauce thicken slightly.

steps.title: Finish with chili crunch
steps.content: Finish with Momofuku Chili Crunch to taste.

steps.title: Plate
steps.content: Serve over rice and top with sesame seeds.

notes.title: Vegetable swaps
notes.body: Any quick-cooking vegetables can be substituted for the carrots and cabbage.

notes.title: Heat dial
notes.body: Adjust the chili crunch to your preferred heat level.

recipes.title: Bacon Egg & Cheese Rice Paper Spiral
recipes.description: A crispy, gooey, melty breakfast treat inspired by NYC bodega bacon egg and cheese sandwiches.

steps.title: Scramble
steps.content: Scramble 4 eggs until just set, soft and fluffy — not dry. Set aside.

steps.title: Prep rice paper
steps.content: Whisk the remaining egg on a plate — this is your egg dip. One at a time, dip each rice paper sheet into the beaten egg, coating evenly. Lay them out on a lightly oiled cutting board, slightly overlapping to create one large sheet.

steps.title: Layer fillings
steps.content: Layer the scrambled eggs down the center, followed by chopped bacon and shredded mozzarella.

steps.title: Roll & shape
steps.content: Roll up tightly into a cylinder, sealing the edge as you go. Then gently curl it around itself into a compact spiral.

steps.title: Season
steps.content: Brush the top with any leftover egg and sprinkle generously with everything bagel seasoning.

steps.title: Bake
steps.content: Bake at 400°F for 15–20 minutes until golden and crisp.

notes.title: Tip
notes.body: Work quickly with the egg-dipped rice paper before it gets too sticky.

notes.title: Bacon prep
notes.body: Make sure your bacon is fully cooked and chopped before starting.

recipes.title: Bread & Butter Pickles
recipes.description: Chef John's classic refrigerator pickle — sweet, tangy, with a slow turmeric warmth. Makes about 2 pints.

ingredients.name: pickling cucumbers (or other firm, small cucumbers)

steps.title: Slice and salt
steps.content: Slice cucumbers into ¼-inch thick rounds. Combine in a large bowl with the sliced onion and jalapeños. Toss with the kosher salt, cover, and let sit at room temperature for 2 hours. This draws out excess moisture for crunchier pickles.

steps.title: Drain
steps.content: After 2 hours, drain the cucumbers well in a colander. Do not rinse. Pat dry with paper towels if desired.

steps.title: Make the brine
steps.content: In a saucepan, combine the vinegar, sugar, water, mustard seeds, celery seeds, peppercorns, turmeric, cloves, and garlic. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar.

steps.title: Combine
steps.content: Add the drained cucumber mixture to the hot brine. Stir to combine and bring just back to a simmer.

steps.title: Jar
steps.content: Transfer the pickles and brine to clean mason jars, making sure the cucumbers are fully submerged in liquid. Let cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Refrigerate
steps.content: Cover and refrigerate. The pickles are ready to eat after 24 hours but improve with a few days of resting. Best flavor develops after 1 week.

notes.title: Storage
notes.body: Keeps refrigerated for several months.

notes.title: Sugar
notes.body: Can reduce to 1–1.5 cups for less sweet pickles.

notes.title: Heat
notes.body: Jalapeños are optional; omit for milder pickles.

notes.title: Canning
notes.body: For shelf-stable pickles, process in a water bath for 10 minutes. Refrigerator pickles need only soap-and-water cleaning of jars.

recipes.title: Caramelized Onion Pasta
recipes.description: Jammy onions, chili crisp, cream, and a heavy parmesan finish. The original cream version — silky and rich.

steps.title: Mise en place
steps.content: Slice your onion, mince the garlic (use fresh), and measure out all your seasonings. Bring the cream or coconut milk to room temperature.

steps.title: Caramelize
steps.content: Heat 2 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the onions and let them cook for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and jammy. If they stick, hit them with a splash of water.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.content: While onions caramelize, boil a pot of salted water and cook pasta until al dente. Drain, but reserve some pasta water — liquid gold.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.content: When onions are deeply golden, stir in the garlic and seasonings. Bloom for a minute, add chili crisp and sauté another minute. Pour in cream (or coconut milk). Simmer for a few minutes, then add the parmesan.

steps.title: Toss
steps.content: Add pasta to the sauce and toss to coat. Use reserved pasta water to loosen if too thick — silky, not sticky.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Serve hot with an extra spoon of chili crisp on top and parsley if you're feeling fancy.

notes.title: Onion patience
notes.body: 15–20 minutes of caramelization is the floor, not the ceiling. Deep golden = deep flavor.

recipes.title: Caramelized Onion Pasta
recipes.description: Same jammy onions and chili crisp, but with blended cottage cheese standing in for cream. ~25g extra protein, no one will know.

steps.title: Mise en place
steps.content: Slice onion, mince garlic, measure seasonings. Blend cottage cheese and skim milk until completely smooth — this is your creamy base.

steps.title: Caramelize
steps.content: Heat butter + olive oil over medium. Add onions and cook 15–20 minutes until golden and jammy. Splash with water if they stick.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.content: Boil pasta to al dente in salted water. Reserve some pasta water before draining.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.content: Stir garlic and seasonings into golden onions, bloom for a minute. Add chili crisp, sauté one more minute. REMOVE FROM HEAT, let cool 1–2 minutes (this prevents curdling), then pour in the blended cottage cheese mixture. Stir, return to LOW heat, warm through gently — do not boil. Add parmesan.

steps.title: Toss
steps.content: Add pasta and toss. Loosen with reserved pasta water as needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Top with extra chili crisp and parsley.

notes.title: Protein boost
notes.body: The cottage cheese swap adds roughly 25g of protein to the entire dish compared to the cream version.

notes.title: Key tip
notes.body: Blend cottage cheese until silky smooth — no one will know it's there. Let the pan cool slightly before adding it to prevent curdling.

recipes.title: Chicken Gnocchi Soup
recipes.description: Creamy, cozy, one-pot. Chicken seared in sun-dried tomato oil, finished with cream, gnocchi, spinach, basil, and a parmesan rind.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.content: Toss the chicken with sun-dried tomato oil and all the chicken seasonings. Let it marinate for as long as your patience can handle — or go straight to the pot.

steps.title: Sear
steps.content: Heat 4 tbsp olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook until nicely browned on both sides. It should not yet be cooked through. Remove and set aside.

steps.title: Sweat the vegetables
steps.content: In the same pot, add onion, celery, carrots, sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, and all veggie seasonings. Cook over medium for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until everything is soft. Stir in tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the broth
steps.content: Pour in chicken broth and bring to a gentle simmer for 15 minutes. While it simmers, chop or shred the chicken. Add the chicken back, then slowly stir in the cream. Simmer another 5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.content: Add gnocchi, parmesan, parmesan rind (if using), spinach, basil, and thyme. Squeeze in lemon juice. Simmer 5–10 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Ladle into bowls and finish with black pepper, chili flakes, extra parmesan, and more basil. Serve with warm buttered bread.

notes.title: Cream temperature
notes.body: Bring cream to room temp before adding to prevent the soup from breaking when it hits the hot broth.

recipes.title: Chicken Protein Cheese Dip
recipes.description: Cottage-cheese-blended cheese dip with chunk chicken, Hatch chilies, and adobo. Tailgate-friendly, weirdly high protein.

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.content: Add cottage cheese, Trader Joe's Three Cheese Blend, taco seasoning, water, and jalapeños with juice to a blender. Blend until smooth.

steps.title: Transfer
steps.content: Transfer blended cheese mixture to a sauce pot over medium heat.

steps.title: Add proteins
steps.content: Add the can of chunk chicken and the can of Hatch green chilies to the pot.

steps.title: Season
steps.content: Season with adobo peppers, salt, garlic, garlic powder, onion powder, and a small amount of cayenne to taste.

steps.title: Heat through
steps.content: Stir to combine and heat through until warmed and well incorporated. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Coconut Macaroons
recipes.description: Soft and chewy on the inside, crisp and golden on the outside. Optional chocolate-dipped finish.

ingredients.name: sweetened flaked coconut (Baker's Angel Flake recommended)
sweetened condensed milk (¾ cup plus 2 tbsp)

steps.title: Preheat
steps.content: Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Set two oven racks near the center. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

steps.title: Mix coconut base
steps.content: In a medium bowl, mix together the coconut, sweetened condensed milk, and vanilla extract. Set aside.

steps.title: Whip whites
steps.content: In the bowl of an electric mixer, beat the egg whites and salt until stiff peaks form.

steps.title: Fold
steps.content: Use a large rubber spatula to fold the egg whites into the coconut mixture until combined.

steps.title: Scoop
steps.content: Using a mini ice cream scoop or two spoons, form heaping tablespoons of the mixture into mounds on the prepared baking sheets, spacing about 1 inch apart.

steps.title: Bake
steps.content: Bake for 23–25 minutes, rotating the pans from top to bottom and front to back halfway through, until tops and edges are golden.

steps.title: Cool
steps.content: Let cool on the pans for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

steps.title: Optional: chocolate dip
steps.content: Melt chocolate in a microwave-safe bowl at medium power, 30-second intervals, until smooth. Dip the bottoms of cooled macaroons, return to the lined sheets, refrigerate 10 minutes to set.

notes.title: Parchment, not wax
notes.body: Macaroons stick to wax paper. Use parchment.

notes.title: Coconut brand
notes.body: Baker's Angel Flake is recommended — there's variability between brands.

notes.title: Storage
notes.body: Keeps in an airtight container at room temp for about a week.

notes.title: Freezing
notes.body: Freeze undipped for up to 3 months. Thaw before dipping in chocolate.

recipes.title: GF Air Fryer Fried Chicken
recipes.description: Double-dredge cornstarch + crushed cornflakes for maximum crunch and adhesion. Fully gluten-free, finished with a sweet-savory honey garlic ginger dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs or breast
cornstarch (divided: ½ cup for dredge, ¼ cup for cornflake mix)
salt (½ tsp for chicken, ½ tsp for dredge)

steps.title: Prep the chicken
steps.content: Cut chicken into strips or chunks. For whole thighs or breasts, pound to 1-inch thickness or butterfly. Pat completely dry. Season directly with half the salt and pepper. Let rest 10–15 min at room temp.

steps.title: Set up breading stations
steps.content: Crush cornflakes to medium (panko-sized) consistency. Dish 1: ½ cup cornstarch + remaining salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, cayenne. Dish 2: beaten eggs. Dish 3: crushed cornflakes + remaining ¼ cup cornstarch.

steps.title: Double dredge
steps.content: Cornstarch (Dish 1, shake off excess) → egg (Dish 2, drip off) → cornflake mix (Dish 3, press firmly all sides). Place coated pieces on a wire rack while preparing the rest.

steps.title: Air fry — first side
steps.content: Preheat air fryer to 385°F for 3–5 min. Arrange chicken in a single layer with space between pieces. Spray tops generously. Cook 8 minutes.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.content: Flip carefully, spray again, cook 8 more minutes (16 total for 1-inch pieces). Verify internal temp reaches 165°F.

steps.title: Rest
steps.content: Transfer to a wire rack over a sheet pan. Rest 4–6 minutes — lets steam escape, prevents sogginess.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.content: Combine honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes in a small saucepan. Heat over medium-low about 3 minutes, stirring, until combined. Keep warm.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Serve chicken with sauce on the side for dipping. Coating it directly will soften the crust.

notes.title: Why double dredge
notes.body: The cornstarch in the final coating gives the cornflakes something to grip. Single dredge works but adhesion is better.

notes.title: Cornflake consistency
notes.body: Aim for panko-sized pieces. Too fine loses texture; too coarse won't adhere.

notes.title: Oil spray is essential
notes.body: Without it, cornflakes stay pale and chewy rather than golden and crisp.

notes.title: Verify GF
notes.body: Check that your cornflakes and soy sauce are certified gluten-free.

notes.title: Bone-in adjustment
notes.body: For bone-in pieces, increase cook time to 22–28 minutes total, flipping halfway.

recipes.title: GF French Beef Stew
recipes.description: Classic French beef stew with mushrooms — adapted GF using tapioca starch in place of flour. Long simmer, glossy finish.

steps.title: Crisp the bacon
steps.content: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium. Add bacon and cook until crisp. Remove and set aside.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.content: Season the beef chunks with salt and pepper. In the same pot, brown in batches to ensure each piece is well-seared. Remove and set aside with the bacon.

steps.title: Sweat aromatics
steps.content: In the same pot, add chopped onion, sliced carrots, and minced garlic. Cook until onion becomes translucent.

steps.title: Thicken with starch
steps.content: Sprinkle the tapioca starch over the vegetables and stir well, ensuring even coating and scraping the fond off the bottom of the pot.

steps.title: Combine and simmer
steps.content: Return beef and bacon to the pot. Stir in tomato paste, add bouquet garni. Pour in beef broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for about 2 hours.

steps.title: Mushrooms
steps.content: About 30 minutes before the stew is done, sauté mushrooms in oil in a separate pan until golden. Add to the stew and continue to simmer.

notes.title: Flour swap
notes.body: Tapioca starch is a clean 1:1 substitute — thickens without going gummy and leaves the broth glossy. Arrowroot or potato starch break down over long simmers; if using those, stir in as a slurry during the last 30 minutes.

notes.title: Bacon
notes.body: Look for a GF-certified label or check the ingredient list — flavorings/smoke additives can introduce gluten.

notes.title: Beef broth
notes.body: Store-bought broths sometimes contain hydrolyzed wheat protein. Use GF-certified or homemade.

recipes.title: Homemade Gyros Salad
recipes.description: Air-fryer gyro meat (food-processor smooth) over romaine with tzatziki, feta, and a red wine vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: English cucumber (grated and squeezed very dry)

steps.title: Process the meat
steps.content: Blend all meat ingredients in a food processor until it becomes a smooth, sticky paste — this is what gives you the dense, sliceable texture.

steps.title: Air-fry
steps.content: Spread thin (~¼ inch) on parchment in your air fryer. Cook at 375°F for 12–15 minutes, flipping halfway. Browned and slightly crispy at the edges.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.content: Let rest a few minutes, then slice into strips.

steps.title: Tzatziki
steps.content: Combine all tzatziki ingredients. Letting it sit for 30 minutes improves the flavor significantly.

steps.title: Build the salad
steps.content: Build on a bed of chopped romaine with tomatoes, red onion, cucumber, olives, pepperoncini, feta, and parsley.

steps.title: Dress and top
steps.content: Drizzle with a simple red wine vinaigrette (3:1 olive oil to red wine vinegar, pinch of oregano, salt, pepper). Top with warm gyro meat strips and a generous dollop of tzatziki. Warm pita on the side if you want.

notes.title: Texture key
notes.body: The food processor paste is what gives sliceable, dense gyro meat. Don't skip the processing step.

recipes.title: Ken's Meat Sauce
recipes.description: A slow-simmered Sunday sauce — thyme, marjoram, rosemary, capers with their brine, lemon, and red wine vinegar bring layered acid and lift.

steps.title: Sweat the onion
steps.content: Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium / medium-low. Add onions with a pinch of salt and cook ~5 minutes until translucent.

steps.title: Garlic
steps.content: Add garlic and cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.content: Increase heat to medium. Add ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains.

steps.title: Toast herbs
steps.content: Create a well in the center of the meat. Add thyme, marjoram, and rosemary to the well and toast until fragrant, ~30 seconds, then stir into the meat.

steps.title: Tomato paste
steps.content: Add tomato paste to the well and cook for 1 minute, stirring to incorporate.

steps.title: Crushed tomato + acids
steps.content: Add crushed tomatoes and stir. Add red wine vinegar, capers with juice, lemon juice. Stir well.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.content: Add bay leaves, bring to a low boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 3–4 hours, stirring occasionally. Add chicken stock as needed to maintain consistency.

steps.title: Finish
steps.content: Remove bay leaves (and herb sprigs if using fresh) before serving. Adjust salt to taste.

notes.title: The simmer is non-negotiable
notes.body: The long simmer is essential — it allows the acids to mellow, flavors to marry, and the sauce to develop body. Don't rush it.

recipes.title: Rosemary Breakfast Potatoes
recipes.description: Crispy, herb-loaded breakfast potatoes — boiled first for a fluffy interior, then roasted at high convection heat for maximum crunch.

steps.title: Cut
steps.content: Halve each potato lengthwise, then halve each half lengthwise again (into quarters). Cut crosswise into ¼–⅓-inch thick slices.

steps.title: Boil
steps.content: Place potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, salt generously. Bring to a boil and cook until soft and tender throughout but not falling apart, ~10–12 minutes.

steps.title: Drain and season
steps.content: Drain well and return to the pot or a large bowl. Drizzle with olive oil and toss gently. Add salt, pepper, rosemary, garlic powder, and onion salt. Toss until evenly seasoned.

steps.title: Roast — first side
steps.content: Spread in a single layer on a sheet pan. Roast at 460°F convection for 15 minutes until bottoms are golden and crispy.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.content: Flip and roast 15 more minutes until deeply golden and crisp on both sides.

notes.title: Why boil-then-roast
notes.body: Boiling gelatinizes the starch so you get a creamy interior; the high convection heat crisps the edges fast.

notes.title: Slice thinness
notes.body: Keep slices thin (¼–⅓ inch) so they get plenty of surface area for browning.

notes.title: No convection?
notes.body: Bump the temp to 475°F and you may need a couple extra minutes per side.

recipes.title: Steak Bites with Cottage Cheese Alfredo
recipes.description: Cast-iron seared steak cubes over fettuccine with a blender-only cottage-cheese alfredo. Higher protein, lower fat than a butter/cream/parm classic.

ingredients.name: light cream cheese (or ~6 wedges Laughing Cow Light)
garlic powder (preferred — or 2–3 fresh garlic cloves)

steps.title: Season the steak
steps.content: Pat steak cubes dry. Toss with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and parsley until evenly coated. Let sit at room temp while you prep the sauce.

steps.title: Blend the alfredo
steps.content: Add cottage cheese, cream cheese, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and parsley to a high-speed blender. Blend on high for 3–5 minutes until completely smooth and warmed through — friction heats the sauce as it emulsifies.

steps.title: Heat the cast iron
steps.content: Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat (or preheat grill to high) until smoking. No oil needed if cast iron is well-seasoned; otherwise a teaspoon of high-smoke-point oil.

steps.title: Sear
steps.content: Sear steak cubes in a single layer, ~60–90 seconds per side for medium-rare. Work in batches if needed — do not crowd the pan or they'll steam. Transfer to a plate and let rest 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.content: Start cooking the pasta to al dente while the steak rests. Reserve ½ cup pasta water before draining.

steps.title: Toss
steps.content: Toss drained pasta with alfredo sauce, thinning with a splash of pasta water if needed for desired consistency.

steps.title: Plate
steps.content: Plate pasta, top with steak bites, drizzle any resting juices over the top, finish with parsley. Serve immediately.

notes.title: Garlic powder > fresh
notes.body: Blends smoother into a no-cook (blender-only) alfredo and avoids the raw bite that fresh garlic gives.

notes.title: Cream cheese swap
notes.body: Laughing Cow Light wedges work as the cream cheese swap; ~6 wedges ≈ 150g. Slightly tangier but the difference disappears once seasoned.

notes.title: Blender warming
notes.body: High-speed blender (Vitamix-class) for several minutes brings the sauce to serving temp without splitting. Lower-power blenders may need a quick warm in a saucepan after.

notes.title: Steak temp
notes.body: 60–90 sec/side for medium-rare on ¾" cubes. Add ~30 sec/side per doneness step.

notes.title: Macro angle
notes.body: Cottage cheese + light cream cheese yields a sauce that's dramatically higher protein and lower fat than a butter/cream/parm classic.

recipes.title: Sweet Pickled Celery
recipes.description: Inspired by Nomad East in Salt Lake City — bright, sweet, lemon-zest forward. Cured 2 weeks for full flavor.

ingredients.name: lemon zest strip per jar (about 2", no pith)
large bunch celery (sliced on a bias ¼" thick, 6–7 cups)

steps.title: Make brine
steps.content: Combine vinegar, water, sugar, salt, peppercorns, and celery seed in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve.

steps.title: Zest the jars
steps.content: Place one strip of lemon zest in each sterilized pint jar.

steps.title: Pack
steps.content: Pack raw celery tightly into jars, leaving ½" headspace.

steps.title: Brine and de-bubble
steps.content: Ladle hot brine over celery, maintaining ½" headspace. Remove air bubbles with a chopstick or bubble tool.

steps.title: Seal
steps.content: Wipe rims clean, apply lids and bands finger-tight.

steps.title: Process
steps.content: Process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes. (Adjust for altitude: add 5 minutes above 6,000 feet.)

steps.title: Cure
steps.content: Let jars rest 24 hours. Check seals. Cure at least 2 weeks before opening for best flavor.

notes.title: More sweetness
notes.body: Increase sugar to 1¼ cups.

notes.title: Brighter citrus
notes.body: Add a second zest strip or try Meyer lemon.

notes.title: Warmer profile
notes.body: Add a coin of fresh ginger or a cracked cardamom pod.

notes.title: Deeper complexity
notes.body: Substitute ½ cup apple cider vinegar for part of the rice vinegar.
